title: Companies Are Using AI as an Excuse to Fire People Instead of Training Them
description:
The tech industry is pushing massive layoffs while claiming AI will replace workers, but this approach is backwards. Instead of investing in employee training and upskilling on AI tools, companies are taking the cheap route of cutting headcount and hoping technology will magically solve their productivity problems.

This shortsighted strategy ignores a fundamental truth: AI works best when it augments human capabilities, not when it replaces them entirely. The most successful companies will be those that invest in teaching their workforce how to leverage these powerful tools rather than simply eliminating jobs.

We're seeing the early signs that this layoff-heavy approach isn't delivering the promised results. Stock prices aren't soaring just because payroll costs dropped. Real productivity gains come from humans working alongside AI, not from AI working alone.

The companies that figure this out first will have a massive competitive advantage. They'll have skilled teams that know how to maximize AI's potential while maintaining the human insight and creativity that no algorithm can replicate.

What we really need is a cultural shift away from viewing AI as a replacement technology and toward seeing it as an amplification technology. The question isn't whether AI will change work, but whether companies will be smart enough to prepare their people for that change.
